# Disagreement Log — T12_004 (Testament of Judah)
**Chapter:** T12_004 | **Verses:** 11 sections (~26 verses)
**Translators compared:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA | **Arbiter:** SOPHIA

| # | Verse | Issue | EMET | LOGOS | PNEUMA | SOPHIA ruling |
|---|-------|-------|------|-------|--------|---------------|
| 1 | 2:2–8 | Warrior deeds | Detailed with each feat as separate clause | Summarized/condensed | Paraphrased with editorial comment | EMET detail retained; the warrior catalogue is a literary form that should be preserved in full |
| 2 | 4:1 | Order of marriages | "before I took Bathshua...I had taken Tamar" (EMET reversal) | Standard order — Bathshua first, Tamar after | Narrative reordering for clarity | SOPHIA follows LOGOS/PNEUMA chronological order; EMET reversal is awkward |
| 3 | 5:3 | Amorite custom | "the-custom-of-the-Amorites" | "the custom of the Amorites" | Omitted in favor of narrative explanation | Retained — this detail explains Tamar's positioning; PNEUMA omission reduces comprehension |
| 4 | 6:4 | Duration of fasting | "fourteen years" | "fourteen years" | Not specified | "fourteen years" — both EMET and LOGOS agree; PNEUMA omission rejected |
| 5 | 10:2 | Enoch reference | "books-of-Enoch-the-righteous" | "books of Enoch the righteous" | "books of Enoch" | Full title "books of Enoch the righteous" — attested in MS and preserved in 4EZ |
| 6 | 11:4 | Final Messianic climax | "God-and-man" (compound) | "God and man, He shall save all the Gentiles" | "God and man together" | "God and man; he shall save all the nations and the race of Israel" — balances both scopes |

---
*SOPHIA notes: Testament of Judah is the longest of the twelve and most narratively rich. The Tamar episode (sections 5–6) is one of the most candid moral confessions in the corpus. EMET's hyphenated style occasionally obscures the narrative drive; PNEUMA's compression loses important details. The "two contrary passions" formula (10:7) is unanimous across all three translators — a sign of textual clarity in the Greek.*
